speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; I need to ask you a few questions to evaluate your condition properly. 

Do you have any history of polyhydramnios, and has your abdomen appeared distended or palpable masses been noted?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with midgut volvulus. The combination of a newborn age, bilious vomiting, and the specific history of a sibling with pyloric stenosis (indicating a family predisposition to congenital anomalies) strongly points to malrotation. The absence of polyhydramnios or maternal diabetes makes other causes less likely, and the bilious nature of the vomit necessitates ruling out volvulus immediately via an upper GI series.
